title: Coordinates and Straight-Line Graphs: Four Quadrants, Midpoints and y = mx + c
seo_title: Year 7 Coordinates Worksheets: Four Quadrants, Midpoints, x = a, y = b and Straight-Line Graphs
standard_text: Work with coordinates in all four quadrants; recognise, sketch and produce graphs of linear functions of one variable with appropriate scaling, using equations in x and y and the Cartesian plane.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 coordinates worksheets with grids: read coordinates in four quadrants, midpoints and missing corners, lines x = a, y = b, y = x and y = −x, and tables of values for straight-line graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: (x, y): go across first, then up or down.
key_sub: x = 3 is a vertical line and y = 3 is a horizontal line. The midpoint is the mean of the coordinates.
body_html:
How it works

Coordinates are written (x, y): go across first, then up or down. Left of the y-axis, x is negative; below the x-axis, y is negative.

x = 3 is a vertical line; y = 3 is a horizontal line. The midpoint of two points is the mean of the xs and the mean of the ys.

Example

What are the coordinates of B above?

4 to the left, 1 down.

Answer: (−4, −1)

Example

Find the midpoint of (2, 5) and (8, −1).

(2 + 8) ÷ 2 = 5.

(5 + (−1)) ÷ 2 = 2.

Answer: (5, 2)

Example

Find y on the line y = 2x − 1 when x = −3.

2 × (−3) − 1 = −7.

Answer: −7

Common mistakes

  • Swapping the coordinates: (3, 2) is 3 across and 2 up, not 2 across and 3 up.
  • Forgetting a negative sign for points left of or below the axes.
  • Thinking x = 3 is horizontal. It is vertical, because x is always 3.
  • Subtracting instead of adding when finding a midpoint.

faq.q: Which comes first, x or y?
faq.a: x comes first. Go along the corridor, then up (or down) the stairs.

faq.q: What does the line x = 3 look like?
faq.a: A vertical line through 3 on the x-axis. Every point on it has x-coordinate 3.

faq.q: How do I find a midpoint?
faq.a: Add the two x-coordinates and halve, then add the two y-coordinates and halve.

faq.q: How do I know if a point is on a line?
faq.a: Substitute the x-coordinate into the equation. If you get the y-coordinate, the point is on the line.

items.q: In which quadrant is the point (5, 2)?
items.e: x is positive and y is positive, so the point is first (top right).

items.q: In which quadrant is the point (−2, 4)?
items.e: x is negative and y is positive, so the point is second (top left).

items.q: In which quadrant is the point (4, 5)?

items.q: In which quadrant is the point (−4, −3)?
items.e: x is negative and y is negative, so the point is third (bottom left).

items.q: Find the midpoint of (−4, −1) and (−4, −9).
items.e: Add the xs and halve, add the ys and halve: (−8 ÷ 2, −10 ÷ 2) = (−4, −5).

items.q: Find the midpoint of (−1, 5) and (7, −1).
items.e: Add the xs and halve, add the ys and halve: (6 ÷ 2, 4 ÷ 2) = (3, 2).

items.q: Find the midpoint of (−2, 2) and (2, −4).
items.e: Add the xs and halve, add the ys and halve: (0 ÷ 2, −2 ÷ 2) = (0, −1).

items.q: Three corners of a square are (4, −2), (4, 3) and (−1, 3). What are the coordinates of the fourth corner?
items.e: The sides are horizontal and vertical, so the missing corner shares an x-coordinate with one corner and a y-coordinate with another: (−1, −2).

items.q: Three corners of a square are (−4, −1), (1, 4) and (−4, 4). What are the coordinates of the fourth corner?
items.e: The sides are horizontal and vertical, so the missing corner shares an x-coordinate with one corner and a y-coordinate with another: (1, −1).

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: The points (1, 1), (2, 2), (−3, −3) are on it: y is the same as x, so y = x.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: Every point on the line has y-coordinate −4, so it is y = −4. Lines y = … are horizontal.

items.q: Which line is horizontal?
items.e: x = a number is a vertical line; y = a number is a horizontal line. So y = −5.

items.e: x = a number is a vertical line; y = a number is a horizontal line. So y = −2.

items.e: On the line x = 5, the x-coordinate is always 5: (5, 0).

sets.title: Tables of values for straight lines

items.q: For the line y = 4x + 3, find y when x = −3.
items.e: Substitute: 4 × (−3) + 3 = −9.

items.q: For the line y = 2x + 3, find y when x = 3.
items.e: Substitute: 2 × 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: For the line y = 2x − 5, find y when x = 0.
items.e: Substitute: 2 × 0 − 5 = −5.

items.q: For the line y = −x + 6, find y when x = 5.
items.e: Substitute: −1 × 5 + 6 = 1.

items.q: For the line y = 0.5x + 2, find y when x = 0.
items.e: Substitute: 0.5 × 0 + 2 = 2.

items.q: For the line y = −2x + 1, find y when x = 0.
items.e: Substitute: −2 × 0 + 1 = 1.

items.q: For the line y = 5x, find y when x = 3.
items.e: Substitute: 5 × 3 + 0 = 15.

items.q: For the line y = 3x + 1, find y when x = 5.
items.e: Substitute: 3 × 5 + 1 = 16.

items.q: For the line y = 3x + 3, find y when x = 3.
items.e: Substitute: 3 × 3 + 3 = 12.

items.q: For the line y = 2x + 5, find y when x = 5.
items.e: Substitute: 2 × 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: For the line y = −2x − 1, find y when x = 0.
items.e: Substitute: −2 × 0 − 1 = −1.

items.q: For the line y = 5x − 1, find y when x = 2.
items.e: Substitute: 5 × 2 − 1 = 9.

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 3x + 1?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 3 × 0 + 1 = 1, which matches. So (0, 1).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 3x?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 3 × 3 + 0 = 9, which matches. So (3, 9).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = x + 1?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 1 × 1 + 1 = 2, which matches. So (1, 2).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 4x + 1?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 4 × 4 + 1 = 17, which matches. So (4, 17).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 3x − 2?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 3 × 2 − 2 = 4, which matches. So (2, 4).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = x − 4?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 1 × (−2) − 4 = −6, which matches. So (−2, −6).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = x − 3?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 1 × (−4) − 3 = −7, which matches. So (−4, −7).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 4x + 4?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 4 × (−3) + 4 = −8, which matches. So (−3, −8).

items.q: Point A is (3, −2). It is moved 4 units left and 5 units up. Where is it now?
Which point is on the y-axis?
items.e: Every point on the y-axis has x = 0: (0, −4).

items.q: Which point is on the x-axis?
items.e: Every point on the x-axis has y = 0: (6, 0).

items.q: Where do the lines x = 3 and y = −2 cross?
items.e: The point has x = 3 and y = −2: (3, −2).

items.q: What is the equation of the x-axis?
items.e: Every point on the x-axis has y-coordinate 0, so it is y = 0.

items.q: The point (k, 7) lies on the line y = 2x + 1. Find k.
The point (−2, m) lies on the line y = 3x + 5. Find m.
A line goes through (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 5) and (3, 7). What is its equation?
items.e: y goes up by 2 each time x goes up by 1, and y = 1 when x = 0: y = 2x + 1.

items.q: Which line does NOT pass through the origin (0, 0)?
items.e: When x = 0, y = x + 1 gives 1, not 0. So y = x + 1.

items.q: A, B and C are (1, 1), (5, 1) and (5, 4). What is the length of AB?
items.e: A and B have the same y, so AB = 5 − 1 = 4 units.

items.q: The midpoint of AB is (2, 3). A is (0, 1). What are the coordinates of B?
items.e: From A to the midpoint is +2 and +2. Do it again: (4, 5).

items.q: Which is the steepest line?
items.e: The number in front of x shows how steep a line is. The biggest is 4: y = 4x.

items.q: Three points are (−1, −1), (2, 2) and (4, 4). Which line are they on?
items.e: Each has y equal to x: y = x.

items.q: Which line is parallel to y = 3?
items.e: y = 3 is horizontal. Another horizontal line is y = −1.

items.q: A square has corners at (1, 1), (4, 1) and (4, 4). What is its area?
items.e: The side is 4 − 1 = 3, so the area is 3 × 3 = 9 square units.

items.q: Complete the table for y = 2x − 3 when x = −1, 0, 1, 2.
What are the coordinates of the midpoint of P and Q?
Which point is on the line shown?
items.e: Follow the line: when x = 3 it crosses the x-axis, so (3, 0).

items.q: A, B and C are three corners of a square. Where is the fourth corner?
items.e: The square has sides of 4. The fourth corner is below A and to the right of C: (2, −1).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: E is 4 to the left on the x-axis: (−4, 0).
